sentences.text: The appellant was convicted for the offence punishable under Section 6 POCSO Act read with Section 5(m) POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 20 years along with payment of fine of Rs. 5,000/-, in default whereof to further undergo simple imprisonment for one month.
The benefit under Section 428 Cr.P.C. was also granted 3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated and that the conviction rests solely on the testimony of the prosecutrix, which suffers from material contradictions and inconsistencies when compared with her earlier statements and the depositions of her mother and sister.
It is urged that the FSL report does not conclusively support the prosecution case.
Learned counsel further submits that the appellant has already undergone more than six years of custody and has maintained good conduct in jail.
4. Learned APP for the State opposes the application and relies upon the testimony of the prosecutrix (PW-2) as well as the corroborative evidence on record, including the FSL report.
It is submitted that the gravity of the offence and the sentence awarded warrant rejection of the application.
5. A perusal of the Trial Court record shows that, the child victim (PW- 2) categorically identified the accused.
She stated that he lured her to a vacant plot on the pretext of giving her chocolates, removed her clothes, closed her mouth, and committed penetrative sexual assault on her.

Her version was corroborated by PW-1 (elder sister) and PW-3 (mother), and further supported by forensic evidence (Ex. PW 14/A) matching the blood found on the accused's t-shirt with the blood sample of the child victim.
The appellant's plea of false implication due to an alleged salary dispute with the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/08/2025 at 21:57:13 victim's father was held to be unsubstantiated, as he neither examined any witness in his defence nor produced any material to support this plea in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
6.

The nominal roll dated 31.07.2025 reflects that the appellant has undergone 6 years, 10 months and 21 days of custody (including undertrial period) as on 30.07.2025, has earned remission of 2 months and 12 days, and the unexpired portion of the sentence is 12 years and 10 months and 27 days.
7.
Having gone through the testimony of the child victim as well as FSL report and also looking into the nominal roll, I am not inclined to suspend the sentence of the appellant at this stage.
8. The application is, accordingly, dismissed.
